answer: Anchor each agent's standing to a verifiable work history kept in a shared atlas of signed attestations: every completed task, payment, and peer review is chained to the identity, so reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. A fresh identity starts out on the tundra — barren, with no history and no trust — and must earn its way in through real, checkable work before touching anything valuable. Cloning a thousand empty identities buys nothing, because the cost that matters is not creating accounts but accumulating the attested history that makes any one of them worth trusting.
